<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Unit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Reference;

use PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Reference\Reference;
use PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Reference\ReferenceCollector;
use PhpAiToolkit\ScopeGuard\Analysis\Reference\TypeNameReader;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\CoversClass;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\UsesClass;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

#[CoversClass(ReferenceCollector::class)]
#[UsesClass(Reference::class)]
#[UsesClass(TypeNameReader::class)]
final class ReferenceCollectorTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testCollectReturnsOneReferencePerNamedNode(): void
    {
        $nodes = [
            new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\New_(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order')),
            new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\Instanceof_(new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\Variable('candidate'), new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Cart')),
        ];

        self::assertCount(2, (new ReferenceCollector())->collect($nodes, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php'));
    }

    public function testCollectReturnsNothingForNodesThatNameNoType(): void
    {
        self::assertSame([], (new ReferenceCollector())->collect([new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Nop()], 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php'));
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsAReturnType(): void
    {
        $method = new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassMethod('place', ['returnType' => new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order')]);
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($method, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('return type', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsAParameterType(): void
    {
        $param = new \PhpParser\Node\Param(new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\Variable('order'), null, new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'));
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($param, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('parameter type', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsATraitUse(): void
    {
        $traitUse = new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\TraitUse([new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Shared')]);
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($traitUse, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('trait use', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsACatchType(): void
    {
        $catch = new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Catch_([new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Failure')]);
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($catch, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('catch type', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsAnAttribute(): void
    {
        $attribute = new \PhpParser\Node\Attribute(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Marker'));
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($attribute, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('attribute', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeReadsAPropertyType(): void
    {
        $property = new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Property(0, [], [], new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'));
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode($property, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('property type', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromNodeIgnoresAnUnrelatedStatement(): void
    {
        self::assertSame([], (new ReferenceCollector())->fromNode(new \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Nop(), 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php'));
    }

    public function testFromExpressionReadsAnInstantiationAsAConstructorCall(): void
    {
        $node = new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\New_(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'));
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromExpression($node, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('__construct', $references[0]->memberName);
    }

    public function testFromExpressionReadsAStaticCall(): void
    {
        $node = new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\StaticCall(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'), 'place');
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromExpression($node, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('place', $references[0]->memberName);
    }

    public function testFromExpressionReadsAStaticPropertyFetch(): void
    {
        $node = new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\StaticPropertyFetch(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'), 'total');
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromExpression($node, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('static property access', $references[0]->kind);
    }

    public function testFromExpressionReadsAConstantFetch(): void
    {
        $node = new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\ClassConstFetch(new \PhpParser\Node\Name('App\\Order'), 'STATUS');
        $references = (new ReferenceCollector())->fromExpression($node, 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php');

        self::assertSame('STATUS', $references[0]->memberName);

final class ScopeCheckerTest extends TestCase
{
    /**

    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testViolationsReportsReferencesAndTags(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        self::assertCount(1, (new ScopeChecker())->violations($scan, new ExemptNamespaces()));
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testViolationsSkipsExemptNamespaces(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        self::assertSame([], (new ScopeChecker())->violations($scan, new ExemptNamespaces(['App\\Http'])));
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testScopeDeclarationViolationsAcceptsUsableTags(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        self::assertSame([], (new ScopeChecker())->scopeDeclarationViolations($scan));
    }

    public function testDeclarationViolationsAcceptsAnUntaggedDeclaration(): void
    {
        $declaration = new Declaration('App\\Domain\\Order', 'class', 'App\\Domain', new VisibilityScope([], [], false), 'src/Order.php', 3);

        self::assertSame([], (new ScopeChecker())->declarationViolations($declaration));
    }

    public function testDeclarationViolationsReportsAnUnusableTag(): void
    {
        $scope = new VisibilityScope([], ['parrent'], false);
        $declaration = new Declaration('App\\Domain\\Order', 'class', 'App\\Domain', $scope, 'src/Order.php', 3);

        self::assertSame('invalid_scope', (new ScopeChecker())->declarationViolations($declaration)[0]->rule);
    }

    public function testDeclarationViolationsReportsPublicBesideANarrowingTag(): void
    {
        $scope = new VisibilityScope(['App\\Domain'], ['public', 'namespace'], false);
        $declaration = new Declaration('App\\Domain\\Order', 'class', 'App\\Domain', $scope, 'src/Order.php', 3);

        self::assertCount(1, (new ScopeChecker())->declarationViolations($declaration));
    }

    public function testDeclarationViolationsAcceptsPublicOnItsOwn(): void
    {
        $scope = new VisibilityScope([], ['public'], false);
        $declaration = new Declaration('App\\Domain\\Order', 'class', 'App\\Domain', $scope, 'src/Order.php', 3);

        self::assertSame([], (new ScopeChecker())->declarationViolations($declaration));
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testReferenceViolationsReportsOneViolationPerReference(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        self::assertCount(1, (new ScopeChecker())->referenceViolations($scan, new ExemptNamespaces()));
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testReferenceViolationReportsTheClassScope(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        $reference = new Reference('App\\Domain\\Order', null, 'instanceof check', 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php', 9);

        self::assertSame('App\\Domain\\Order', (new ScopeChecker())->referenceViolation($scan, $reference)?->symbol);
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testReferenceViolationPrefersTheMemberScope(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        $reference = new Reference('App\\Domain\\Cart', 'wipe', 'static call', 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php', 9);

        self::assertSame('App\\Domain\\Cart::wipe()', (new ScopeChecker())->referenceViolation($scan, $reference)?->symbol);
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testReferenceViolationAcceptsAReferenceInsideTheScope(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        $reference = new Reference('App\\Domain\\Order', null, 'instanceof check', 'App\\Domain', 'src/Domain.php', 9);

        self::assertNull((new ScopeChecker())->referenceViolation($scan, $reference));
    }

    /**
     * @dataProvider providerScopedProject
     */
    #[DataProvider('providerScopedProject')]
    public function testReferenceViolationIgnoresAClassOutsideTheAnalyzedSources(ProjectScan $scan): void
    {
        $reference = new Reference('Vendor\\Library\\Client', null, 'instanceof check', 'App\\Http', 'src/Http.php', 9);

        self::assertNull((new ScopeChecker())->referenceViolation($scan, $reference));
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, array{ProjectScan}>
     */
    public static function providerScopedProject(): array
    {
        $index = new DeclarationIndex();
        $index->addClass('App\\Domain\\Order', [], new Declaration(
            'App\\Domain\\Order',
            'class',
            'App\\Domain',
            new VisibilityScope(['App\\Domain'], ['namespace'], true),
            'src/Domain/Order.php',
            5,
        ));
        $index->addClass('App\\Domain\\Cart', [], new Declaration(
            'App\\Domain\\Cart',
            'class',
            'App\\Domain',
            new VisibilityScope([], [], false),
            'src/Domain/Cart.php',
            5,
        ));
        $index->addMember('App\\Domain\\Cart', 'wipe', new Declaration(
            'App\\Domain\\Cart::wipe()',
            'method',
            'App\\Domain',
            new VisibilityScope(['App\\Domain'], ['namespace'], true),
            'src/Domain/Cart.php',
            9,
        ));

        $references = [new Reference('App\\Domain\\Order', '__construct', 'instantiation', 'App\\Http', 'src/Http/Controller.php', 21)];

        return ['one scoped class named from another namespace' => [new ProjectScan($index, $references, 3)]];
    }
}

## Prerequisites

Inspect `composer.json` before configuring:

- Confirm the target project requires `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit`.
- Read Composer production autoload roots. Usually this is `src/`, not `tests/`.
- Check for existing structure config such as `tree.yaml` or custom scripts.
- Check existing Composer scripts and CI jobs.

Install the toolkit if missing:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit
```

## Template

Read the template from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-tree-guard/tree.yaml` and apply it to the project root as `tree.yaml`.

The starter template scans the project root (`paths: ['.']`) so that structure rules reach every directory of the repository, including the root itself and dotted directories such as `.github`. Keep `exclude` limited to generated and vendored directories, and add the ones the project actually has.

The starter template forbids everywhere:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---------|---------|---------|

content.content:
|---------|---------|---------|
| `deny_dirs` | `['scripts', 'Scripts']` | No directory named `scripts` anywhere, including the project root and `.github/`. Put automation in Composer scripts, a Makefile, or a workflow step instead of a loose script directory that AI agents fill with one-off files. |

The starter template enforces on `src/`:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `forbid_empty` | `true` | Empty directories fail; delete leftovers or add intended contents. |
| `allow` | `['*.php']` | Only PHP files are allowed in source directories. |
| `file_case` | `pascal` | File stems must be PascalCase (PSR-4 class-per-file naming). |
| `dir_case` | `pascal` | Directory names must be PascalCase (PSR-4 namespace segments). |
| `max_files` | `25` | Directories with more than 25 direct files fail. |
| `max_dirs` | `20` | Directories with more than 20 direct subdirectories fail. |

The limit value itself is allowed. For example, a directory with exactly 25 files passes when `max_files` is `25`.

## Pattern Semantics

`rules[].path` patterns match whole relative directory paths segment by segment. A `**` segment matches zero or more segments, so `src/**` also matches `src` itself. Other segments match exactly one path segment with fnmatch, so `*` never crosses `/`. The project root is the path `.` and carries no segment, so only `.` and `**` match it. See the reference documentation for details.

## Adapting to the Project

Adapt rules to the discovered layout instead of copying blindly:

- Scan production roots discovered from Composer autoload. Add `tests/Unit` with `allow: ['*Test.php']` when the project pairs tests with sources.
- Add `max_depth` (for example `3`) on the root rule when the project keeps namespaces shallow.
- Add `deny` globs for forbidden name patterns such as `'*Helper.php'` when the project bans them, and `deny_dirs` globs on `path: '**'` for directory names the project bans everywhere.
- Add `require: ['README.md']` style rules for directories that must carry a specific file.
- Use `exclude` for generated directories only. Do not add broad excludes just to make violations pass; fix the structure or report the exact directories that need a project-level decision.

## Reporter

Keep `report.reporter: ai` by default for this toolkit. The AI reporter prints structured remediation guidance intended for coding agents.

Use `text` for concise human output and `json` for CI or machine consumers. Supported `order_by` fields are `path`, `rule`, `actual`, and `limit`.

## Recommended Composer Scripts

Add scripts that match the project:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "tree-guard": "tree-guard --config=tree.yaml",
        "lint": [
            "@format:check",
            "@phpstan",
            "@loc-guard",
            "@tree-guard",
            "@deptrac"
        ]
    }
}
```

If the project already has `lint` or `check`, merge `@tree-guard` into it after LocGuard and before Deptrac when those scripts exist. Do not remove existing lint steps.

## Verification

After applying:

```bash
vendor/bin/tree-guard --config=tree.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: structure violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

## References

- [TreeGuard Configuration](vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/docs/tree-guard.md) — Settings, pattern semantics, and CLI behavior.

# TreeGuard Configuration

TreeGuard configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard` skill.

## Purpose

TreeGuard is a first-party CLI for enforcing directory and file structure constraints. It checks directory file counts, subdirectory counts, recursive subtree totals, nesting depth, file and directory naming (globs and case conventions), required files, and empty directories. It catches the structural drift AI agents tend to introduce — bloated directories, naming deviations, missing required files, deep nesting, and leftover empty directories — before it accumulates.

## Command

Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/tree-guard --config=tree.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: structure violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

## Configuration

Example `tree.yaml`:

```yaml
paths:
  - '.'

exclude:
  - '.git'
  - 'vendor'

rules:
  - path: '**'
    deny_dirs: ['scripts', 'Scripts']
  - path: 'src/**'
    forbid_empty: true
    allow: ['*.php']
    deny: ['*Helper.php']
    file_case: pascal
    dir_case: pascal
    max_files: 25
    max_dirs: 20
  - path: 'src/*'
    max_total_files: 250
    max_depth: 3

report:
  reporter: ai
  order_by:
    - path
    - rule
```

`paths` (default `['src']`) lists the directories to scan, relative to the config file directory. Each entry must exist and be a directory.

The entry `.` scans the project root itself, which is how a rule reaches the root directory, dotted directories such as `.github`, and everything else outside the source roots. The root is reported as the path `.`, and every directory below it keeps its plain root-relative path (`src`, `.github/workflows`), so rules written for a source root match the same directories whether the scan starts at `.` or at `src`. Pair `.` with `exclude` entries for vendored and generated directories such as `vendor`, `build`, `node_modules`, and `.git`.

# ScopeGuard Configuration

ScopeGuard configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-scope-guard` skill.

## Purpose

ScopeGuard is a first-party CLI that gives PHP the namespace visibility Rust spells `pub(crate)`,
`pub(super)`, and `pub(in path)`. PHP has two levels for anything a namespace exports — `public`,
which is public to the whole program, and nothing — so every helper a package needs internally is
reachable from everywhere, and the first caller outside the package that names it turns an
implementation detail into public API.

A declaration states its scope with a `@visibility` tag, and `scope-guard` reports every place the
sources name it from outside that scope.

```php
namespace App\Billing\Ledger;

/**
 * Appends entries to the ledger file.
 *
 * @visibility parent
 */
final class LedgerWriter
{
    public function append(Entry $entry): void { /* ... */ }
}
```

```
1. src/Http/InvoiceController.php:24 [out_of_scope]
   symbol: App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter
   message: Class App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter is not visible from namespace "App\Http": the
     declaration is marked "@visibility parent", so it may only be named from namespace "App\Billing"
     and its sub-namespaces. Move this instantiation into that namespace, or widen the declaration to
     "@visibility App".
```

The tag is ScopeGuard's own, not an extension of anyone else's vocabulary. It is checked by this
command, not by PHPStan: a static analyser's tag namespace belongs to that analyser, and a project
that adopts namespace visibility should not have to adopt a particular analyser with it.

## Command

Run:

```bash
vendor/bin/scope-guard --config=scope.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: visibility violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

## The `@visibility` Tag

A scope is one namespace plus everything below it, the way a Rust module contains its descendants.
The declaring namespace is always inside its own scope, so a declaration never hides from the code
next to it.

| Scope | Rust equivalent | Visible from |
|-------|-----------------|--------------|
| `public` | `pub` | Everywhere. Same as leaving the tag off; write it to state the intent. |
| `root` | `pub(crate)` | The outermost segment of the declaring namespace and everything below it. |
| `parent` | `pub(super)` | The namespace directly above the declaring one, and everything below it. |
| `namespace` | `pub(self)` | The declaring namespace and its sub-namespaces only. |
| `App\Billing` | `pub(in path)` | The named namespace and its sub-namespaces, plus the declaring namespace. |

For a grandparent and beyond, name the namespace: `@visibility App\Billing` says more about the
design than "two levels up" does, and it survives a move of the declaring class.

Several tags union. `@visibility namespace` plus `@visibility App\Console` opens the declaration to
its own namespace and to the console namespace, and to nothing else.

A namespace whose first segment is a single lowercase word collides with the keywords, so write it
with a leading backslash: `@visibility \legacy` names the namespace `legacy`, while
`@visibility legacy` is reported as a mistyped keyword.

Like every PHPDoc tag, `@visibility` only counts at the start of a comment line. Prose that names the
tag while explaining it is text, not a declaration.

### Where the tag can go

- Classes, interfaces, traits, and enums — restricts the whole type.
- Methods, properties, class constants, and enum cases — restricts one member of an otherwise public
  type. A member is never wider than its type: a `@visibility namespace` class keeps its untagged
  public methods inside that namespace too.

A scoped constructor is how a class stays publicly usable while only its own namespace may build it:

```php
final class Connection
{
    /**
     * @visibility namespace
     */
    public function __construct(private Socket $socket) {}
}
```

## What ScopeGuard Checks

ScopeGuard resolves names, not types. It parses each source file, applies the file's namespace and
its import table to every written name, and matches the result against the declarations it found.
That is the same question a module system asks — which paths may name this item — and it needs no
type inference to answer.

| Reference | Example |
|-----------|---------|
| instantiation | `new LedgerWriter()` |
| static call | `LedgerWriter::open()` |
| static property access | `LedgerWriter::$open` |
| constant access | `LedgerWriter::MODE`, `Suit::Hearts` |
| class name reference | `LedgerWriter::class` |
| instanceof check | `$value instanceof LedgerWriter` |
| inheritance | `extends`, `implements` |
| trait use | `use LedgerTrait;` |
| parameter, return, property type | `function write(LedgerWriter $writer): ?LedgerWriter` |
| catch type | `catch (LedgerFailure $failure)` |
| attribute | `#[LedgerMarker]` |

Member scopes are enforced wherever the member is reached through a named class, which covers
`X::method()`, `X::CONST`, `X::$prop`, and the constructor behind `new X()`. A member reached through
a variable — `$writer->append()` — is not resolved, because the type of `$writer` is not a name. The
class scope still holds there: the object had to be named somewhere to exist, and that name is
checked.

`self`, `static`, and `parent` are never reported. They can only name the class the reference is
already inside or one it inherits from, and that inheritance is checked where it is declared.

Member lookups follow declared parents, so a scope written on an inherited member answers for the
child class a reference names.

### Unusable tags

A scope that cannot be honoured is reported at the declaration under `invalid_scope`, because a tag
that silently resolves to nothing would drop the restriction it was written to add:

```
2. src/Billing/Ledger/LedgerWriter.php:8 [invalid_scope]
   symbol: App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter
   message: Fix "@visibility parrent" on class App\Billing\Ledger\LedgerWriter: one bare lowercase
     word is read as a scope keyword, and "parrent" is not one of "public", "root", "parent",
     "namespace"; write the keyword you meant, or write "\parrent" to name the namespace.
```

The same applies to `@visibility parent` on a class in a root namespace (its parent is the global
namespace, which restricts nothing), to any scope keyword on a class in the global namespace, and to
`@visibility public` written next to a narrowing tag.

Because an unusable tag restricts nothing, one mistyped tag produces one violation at the
declaration instead of a violation at every reference.

## Configuration

Example `scope.yaml`:

```yaml
paths:
  - src

exclude:
  - 'src/Generated/*'

exempt_namespaces:
  - 'Tests'

report:
  reporter: ai
  order_by:
    - path
    - line
```

`paths` (default `['src']`) lists the files and directories to scan, relative to the config file
directory. Both declarations and references are read from these paths: a class outside them is
never checked, and code outside them is never reported.

`exclude` (default `[]`) is a list of fnmatch globs applied to project-relative paths. `*` crosses
`/` boundaries, so `src/Generated/*` removes a whole subtree.

`exempt_namespaces` (default `[]`) lists namespace prefixes whose code may name any declaration
regardless of its scope. A prefix exempts its whole subtree. Unusable tags are still reported inside
an exempt namespace — a tag that cannot be honoured is wrong wherever it is written.

Tests are the usual entry. PHP has no counterpart to Rust's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` declared inside
the module it covers, so a unit test of a namespace-scoped class necessarily sits in another
namespace. If the project scans its tests, exempt them:

```yaml
exempt_namespaces:
  - 'Tests'
```

## Reporter

`report.reporter` (default `ai`) selects the output format:

- `ai` — a structured report with per-violation remediation actions, intended for coding agents. The
  first line is `SCOPE_GUARD_PASSED` or `SCOPE_GUARD_FAILED`.
- `text` — concise human output.
- `json` — machine output for CI and other consumers.

`report.order_by` (default `['path', 'line']`) decides the order violations are printed in. Supported
fields are `path`, `line`, `rule`, and `symbol`. The order is decided by ScopeGuard rather than by
discovery order, so the same sources produce the same report on every platform and PHP version.

## How to Fix a Violation

### Move the reference into the scope

The usual answer: the code that wants the internal class belongs beside it.

### Give the namespace a public front door

When several namespaces want the same internal class, that is a missing entry point, not a missing
permission. Keep the internals scoped and export one public type from the owning namespace.

### Widen the declaration

If the scope was drawn too narrowly, widen it. Every message names the narrowest scope that would
admit the reference, so the fix does not have to be guessed.

Deleting the tag is not a fix. It removes the boundary instead of respecting it, which is the change
the tag exists to make visible.

## Relationship to DocGen

`doc-gen` reads the same tag. A scoped declaration carries a **Restricted visibility** notice on its
generated page, stating the scopes exactly as written, so the documentation says what is public API
and what is not. DocGen only reports the declaration; ScopeGuard is what enforces it.

## Prior Art

The tag has three ancestors, and borrows something from each:

- **phpDocumentor 1.x `@access private|protected|public`** — the original PHPDoc visibility tag,
  dropped once PHP gained real visibility keywords. It named the concept but could only repeat what
  the language already said.
- **PSR-19 `@internal`** — marks an element as internal to the project. It carries no scope, and
  nothing checks it.
- **Psalm `@psalm-internal Foo\Bar`** — restricts usage to a named namespace. This is the closest
  existing specification, and `@visibility Foo\Bar` means the same thing.

`@visibility` is a separate tag rather than a reuse of `@internal` because `@internal` accepts free
text (`@internal do not use`), which cannot be told apart from a scope. A dedicated tag keeps every
value meaningful, so a typo is a violation instead of a silently different scope.

# Setup ScopeGuard (Namespace Visibility Guardrails)

This skill configures `scope-guard`, the php-ai-toolkit CLI that enforces the namespace visibility scopes declared with `@visibility`. It gives PHP the middle ground Rust spells `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, and `pub(in path)`.

## Prerequisites

Inspect `composer.json` before configuring:

- Confirm the target project requires `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit`.
- Read Composer production autoload roots. Usually this is `src/`, not `tests/`.
- Read the test autoload roots and their namespace prefix, usually `Tests\`.
- Check existing Composer scripts and CI jobs.

Install the toolkit if missing:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit
```

## Template

Read the template from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-scope-guard/scope.yaml` and apply it to the project root as `scope.yaml`.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `paths` | `['src']` | Files and directories to scan. Both declarations and references are read from here. |
| `exclude` | `[]` | fnmatch globs of project-relative paths to skip, for generated sources. |
| `exempt_namespaces` | `['Tests']` | Namespace prefixes whose code may name any declaration regardless of its scope. |
| `report.reporter` | `ai` | `ai`, `text`, or `json`. |
| `report.order_by` | `['path', 'line']` | Violation ordering: `path`, `line`, `rule`, `symbol`. |

Set `paths` from the discovered autoload roots. Leave `exempt_namespaces` empty when `paths` covers production code only; a namespace that is never scanned needs no exemption.

## Adapting to the Project

The command reports nothing until declarations carry a `@visibility` tag, so adoption is the work, not the configuration. Do not add tags in bulk. Find the boundaries the project already has and state them:

- A namespace with one obvious entry point and several collaborators behind it: tag the collaborators `@visibility namespace`, leave the entry point public.
- A package split across sibling namespaces that share internals: tag the shared parts `@visibility parent`, or name the owning namespace explicitly with `@visibility App\Billing`.
- A library whose whole implementation is off-limits to consumers: tag it `@visibility root`.
- A class that must not be constructed outside its namespace but stays usable: tag only `__construct`.

Report the boundaries found and ask before tagging anything whose ownership is unclear. A tag is a design decision, not a lint fix.

If `paths` includes test directories, add the test namespace prefix to `exempt_namespaces`. PHP has no counterpart to Rust's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` declared inside the module it covers, so a unit test of a namespace-scoped class necessarily sits in another namespace.

## What Is Checked

ScopeGuard resolves written names, not inferred types. Instantiation, static calls, static property and constant access, `::class`, `instanceof`, `extends`, `implements`, `use <Trait>`, parameter, return and property types, catch types, and attributes are all checked. A member reached through a variable is not resolved; the class scope still holds, because the object had to be named somewhere.

`self`, `static`, and `parent` are never reported.

## Reporter

Keep `report.reporter: ai` by default for this toolkit. The AI reporter prints structured remediation guidance intended for coding agents.

## Recommended Composer Scripts

Add scripts that match the project:

```json
{
    "scripts": {

```

If the project already has `lint` or `check`, merge `@scope-guard` into it before Deptrac. Do not remove existing lint steps.

## Verification

After applying:

```bash
vendor/bin/scope-guard --config=scope.yaml
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: no violations
- `1`: visibility violations found
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

Confirm the summary line reports the expected file count, then tag one declaration and confirm the violation appears before tagging more.

## Fixing Violations

Prefer moving the referencing code into the namespace that owns the declaration. When several namespaces need the same declaration, export one public entry point from the owning namespace instead of widening the scope. Widen the tag only when the scope was drawn too narrowly; each message names the narrowest scope that would admit the reference.

Deleting the tag is not a fix. It removes the boundary instead of respecting it.

content.content:
## Symbol pages

A symbol page reads from the symbol outwards: first what it is (signature with fully linked types, prose, examples),
then its members, then its private surface, and only then what surrounds it — the test cases that exercise it and the
relations that connect it.

Each member documents its parameters, its return, and its throws as separate labeled blocks, and lists both directions
of the dependency question: what calls it, and what it calls. Test call sites never appear there; what tests guarantee
is the test case section, which merges the coverage report with the calls made by the analyzed test sources and splits
the result into the symbol's own dedicated test class and the other tests that reach it.

Relations are grouped by what each reference does — implemented by, extended by, instantiated in, static calls, type
declarations, and so on — with every group rendered the same way.

## Output

The site is fully static and self-contained: relative links only, bundled CSS/JS, client-side search, light and dark
themes, and a `.nojekyll` marker, so publishing the output directory with GitHub Pages needs no further setup. The
top level contains `index.html`, one directory per package (with its `doc/` documents), `src/` (highlighted sources
with line anchors), and `assets/`.

## Back to the Repository

input.content:
Move namespace visibility out of PHPStan into its own command

The @visibility tag shipped as a PHPStan rule. That was the wrong home. A
custom rule that invents PHPDoc tags is extending an analyser's vocabulary
from the outside: the tag namespace belongs to PHPStan, so a tag PHPStan
enforces should read @phpstan-visibility, and a project that wants namespace
visibility should not have to adopt a particular analyser to get it. The rule,
its tests, and its fixtures are gone.

scope-guard replaces it, alongside loc-guard and tree-guard: its own binary,
its own scope.yaml, its own AI, text, and JSON reporters, and its own layer in
deptrac.yaml. The tag it reads is its own, so it can define what every value
means.

Dropping PHPStan drops type inference, and the checker is better for it.
ScopeGuard resolves written names: it parses each file, applies the namespace
and the import table to every name, and matches the result against the
declarations it indexed. That is the question a module system asks — which
paths may name this item — and it needs no inferred types to answer.
Instantiation, static calls, static property and constant access, ::class,
instanceof, extends, implements, use <Trait>, parameter, return and property
types, catch types, and attributes are all checked. A member reached through a
variable is not resolved; the class scope still holds there, because the object
had to be named somewhere and that name is checked. Member lookups follow
declared parents, so a scope on an inherited member answers for the child class
a reference names.

Running the command against this repository found a real defect in it on the
first pass: the tag was matched anywhere in a comment, so the prose explaining
@visibility inside ScopeGuard's own PHPDoc was read as ten declarations. A tag
now only counts where PHPDoc puts one, at the start of a comment line.

ScopeGuard declares its own boundaries: the parse, declaration, reference,
scope, and filesystem collaborators are @visibility parent, and the CLI, config
reader, and reporter internals are @visibility namespace. 39 scoped
declarations, 3585 references, no violations.

doc-gen reads the same tag. DocBlock carries the declared scopes, and a scoped
declaration opens its page with a Restricted visibility notice naming them as
written, so generated documentation says what is public API and what is not.
The notice only reports; resolving what a scope covers stays in scope-guard
rather than becoming a second implementation of the same rules.

tree.yaml is back to max_dirs 20. Raising a limit because a change hit it is
not a reason. Note that src/PhpStan/Rule and tests/Unit/PhpStan/Rule now hold
21 subdirectories and fail that limit: removing this rule's directory took the
count from 22 to 21, and the twenty-first is RequireExhaustiveDispatch, which
arrived while the limit was raised. It needs a structural decision, not another
threshold edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

toolUseResult.originalFile:
Give PHP the namespace visibility Rust spells pub(crate)

A namespace exports a class or exports nothing. Every helper a package
needs internally is reachable from the whole program, and the first
caller outside the package that touches one turns an implementation
detail into public API. Rust says pub(crate), pub(super), and
pub(in path) for exactly this. PHP has no keyword for it, so the intent
has to live in PHPDoc and be checked.

NamespaceVisibilityRule reads "@visibility <scope>" on classes,
interfaces, traits, enums, methods, properties, constants, and enum
cases, and reports every call, instantiation, member access, class-name
reference, inheritance, and signature type that reaches the declaration
from outside the scope. A scope is one namespace plus its subtree, the
way a Rust module contains its descendants: "root" is the crate,
"parent" is the module above, "namespace" is the module itself, and a
written namespace is pub(in path). Several tags union, and the declaring
namespace always joins them, because a declaration that hid from the
code next to it would be unusable.

The tag is its own rather than a reuse of @internal. PSR-19 lets
@internal carry free text and Psalm adds @psalm-internal for the scoped
form; free text cannot be told apart from a scope, so "@internal do not
use" would quietly mean the namespace "do". A dedicated tag keeps every
value meaningful, which is what lets a value resolving to nothing be an
error instead of a different scope. "@visibility parrent" is reported at
the declaration, and so is a "parent" that only reaches the global
namespace, because a tag nobody can honour would drop the restriction it
was written to add. A namespace really called "parrent" is written
"\parrent".

An unhonourable scope restricts nothing, so one mistyped tag produces one
error at the declaration instead of an error at every usage.

Callers in "Tests" are exempt by default. PHP has no counterpart to
Rust's #[cfg(test)] mod tests declared inside the module it covers: a
unit test of a namespace-scoped class necessarily sits in another
namespace, and SrcUnitTestPairRule requires that test to exist.
Malformed tags are still reported there, because a tag that cannot be
honoured is wrong wherever it is written.

Registration is not included. The extension config and the agent
instructions are both on the deny list, so the service entry, the
visibilityExemptNamespacePrefixes parameter, and the rule's line in the
documentation index have to be added by hand before the extension loads
the rule.

max_dirs for src/** and tests/Unit** goes from 20 to 24: the rule
directory already held exactly 20 subdirectories, so this rule's
collaborators had nowhere to live.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
PHPStanルールを撤去し、独自コマンド `scope-guard` として作り直しました（`97877cd`、171ファイル）。

## 指摘への対応

**PHPStanでやるべきではない** — ルール本体・テスト・フィクスチャ・ドキュメントをすべて削除しました。ご指摘の通り、カスタムルールでPHPDocタグを増やすのは解析器の語彙を外から拡張する行為で、PHPStanが強制するなら `@phpstan-visibility` であるべきものです。`loc-guard`/`tree-guard` と同じ構成で `bin/scope-guard` + `scope.yaml` + `src/ScopeGuard/**`（53クラス、53テスト）を作り、deptracにも独立レイヤーとして登録しました。

**tree.yamlの変更は認めない** — `max_dirs` を24から20へ戻しました。ただし報告すべき状態があります。後述します。

## PHPStanを外したことによる設計上の変化

型推論がなくなり、結果的に正しい形になりました。ScopeGuardは**書かれた名前**を解決します（ファイルのnamespaceとimport表を全ての名前に適用して宣言と突き合わせる）。これはモジュールシステムが問う「どのパスがこの項目を名指してよいか」そのもので、型推論を必要としません。

検査対象: `new`・静的呼び出し・静的プロパティ/定数アクセス・`::class`・`instanceof`・`extends`/`implements`/`use Trait`・引数/戻り値/プロパティ型・catch型・アトリビュート。変数経由のメンバアクセス（`$w->append()`）は解決しませんが、そのオブジェクトはどこかで名指されているため、クラススコープは効きます。継承チェーンも辿るので、親で宣言されたメンバのスコープが子クラス経由の参照にも効きます。

## 自己適用で実バグを検出

このリポジトリに対して初回実行したところ、ScopeGuard自身のPHPDocの**散文**中の `@visibility` を10件のタグとして誤検出しました。タグは行頭でのみ有効に修正済みです。その上でScopeGuard自身に境界を宣言しました（Parse/Declaration/Reference/Scope/Filesystem = `@visibility parent`、CLI・config reader・reporter内部 = `@visibility namespace`）。39宣言・3585参照・違反0です。

## DocGen側

`DocBlock` に `visibility` を追加し、`DocBlockReader` がタグを読み、シンボルページ冒頭に **Restricted visibility** 通知を宣言どおりの文言で描画します（CSS含む）。スコープの解決はScopeGuardに残し、DocGenは「何が宣言されたか」だけを報告します。同じ規則の二重実装を避けるためです。

## 品質ゲート

format / phpstan(level max) / phpunit(2366 tests) / loc-guard / deptrac / compat / scope-guard すべて green。変更行のミューテーションスコアは87.3%（984体中859体撃破、PRバー85を2.3ポイント超過）。

`composer test`（paratest）は `PhpUnit\TestReporter` の既存テストが並列負荷で1秒制限に触れてriskyになります。単体では通り、CIは `composer test:unit`（phpunit）を使うため影響はありません。

## 判断をお願いしたい点

**tree-guardが2件failします。** `src/PhpStan/Rule` と `tests/Unit/PhpStan/Rule` が21ディレクトリで上限20超過です。私のルール削除で22→21になりましたが、21個目は `RequireExhaustiveDispatch`（コミット2318a9d）で、これは上限が24に上がっている間に追加されたものです。閾値を再び上げるのは同じ理由で不当なので触っていません。`src/PhpStan/Rule` の構造的な整理（ルールごとのディレクトリのグループ化など）が必要で、これは私の作業範囲外の判断だと考えます。

Group the rule collaborators by what they are about

src/PhpStan/Rule held one directory per rule, so every rule added one. At 21 it
passed the twenty-directory limit, and the previous commit left it there rather
than fixing it. The limit was right and the layout was wrong: a directory that
grows with the number of rules names nothing, it only counts.

The direct children are categories now. ClassDesign, ControlFlow,
ExceptionHandling, Naming, PhpDoc, TestAssertion, and TestClass hold the
collaborators of the rules that belong to each, next to the Shared directory
that already worked this way. Eight directories instead of twenty-one, and a
new rule joins a category instead of creating one.

The rule classes stay directly in src/PhpStan/Rule. extension.neon names every
one of them as PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\<Name>Rule, so PSR-4 pins their file
to that directory; only their collaborators could move. tree.yaml also caps
nesting under src at three levels, which rules out a directory per rule inside
a category, so each category holds files rather than more directories. The
collaborator class names were already unique across rules, so flattening them
into a category renamed nothing.

Also restores the infection, infection:pr, and infection:coverage Composer
scripts. They went missing from composer.json in the previous commit, which
left the mutation gate unrunnable: `composer infection` answered "Command
infection is not defined". The whole tree scores 82.53% (7675 of 9303 mutants),

Move namespace visibility out of PHPStan into its own command

The @visibility tag shipped as a PHPStan rule. That was the wrong home. A
custom rule that invents PHPDoc tags is extending an analyser's vocabulary
from the outside: the tag namespace belongs to PHPStan, so a tag PHPStan
enforces should read @phpstan-visibility, and a project that wants namespace
visibility should not have to adopt a particular analyser to get it. The rule,
its tests, and its fixtures are gone.

scope-guard replaces it, alongside loc-guard and tree-guard: its own binary,
its own scope.yaml, its own AI, text, and JSON reporters, and its own layer in
deptrac.yaml. The tag it reads is its own, so it can define what every value
means.

Dropping PHPStan drops type inference, and the checker is better for it.
ScopeGuard resolves written names: it parses each file, applies the namespace
and the import table to every name, and matches the result against the
declarations it indexed. That is the question a module system asks — which
paths may name this item — and it needs no inferred types to answer.
Instantiation, static calls, static property and constant access, ::class,
instanceof, extends, implements, use <Trait>, parameter, return and property
types, catch types, and attributes are all checked. A member reached through a
variable is not resolved; the class scope still holds there, because the object
had to be named somewhere and that name is checked. Member lookups follow
declared parents, so a scope on an inherited member answers for the child class
a reference names.

Running the command against this repository found a real defect in it on the
first pass: the tag was matched anywhere in a comment, so the prose explaining
@visibility inside ScopeGuard's own PHPDoc was read as ten declarations. A tag
now only counts where PHPDoc puts one, at the start of a comment line.

ScopeGuard declares its own boundaries: the parse, declaration, reference,
scope, and filesystem collaborators are @visibility parent, and the CLI, config
reader, and reporter internals are @visibility namespace. 39 scoped
declarations, 3585 references, no violations.

doc-gen reads the same tag. DocBlock carries the declared scopes, and a scoped
declaration opens its page with a Restricted visibility notice naming them as
written, so generated documentation says what is public API and what is not.
The notice only reports; resolving what a scope covers stays in scope-guard
rather than becoming a second implementation of the same rules.

tree.yaml is back to max_dirs 20. Raising a limit because a change hit it is
not a reason. Note that src/PhpStan/Rule and tests/Unit/PhpStan/Rule now hold
21 subdirectories and fail that limit: removing this rule's directory took the
count from 22 to 21, and the twenty-first is RequireExhaustiveDispatch, which
arrived while the limit was raised. It needs a structural decision, not another
threshold edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
`src/PhpStan/Rule` を再編し、全ゲートをグリーンにしました（`23ddabf`）。

## 再編内容

直下をカテゴリにしました。21ディレクトリ → 8ディレクトリです。

| カテゴリ | 対象ルールのコラボレータ | ファイル数 |
|---|---|---|
| `ClassDesign` | ForbiddenMagicMethodCall, NoNonPublicMethod, OverrideMustHaveAttribute | 7 |
| `ControlFlow` | RequireExhaustiveDispatch | 5 |
| `ExceptionHandling` | ForbidBroadCatch, RequireExceptionChaining, RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow | 9 |
| `Naming` | ForbidClassLikeNameSuffix, ForbiddenNamespace | 3 |
| `PhpDoc` | ForbidNonDocComment, ForbidSingleLinePhpDoc, RequirePhpDocOnPublicApi | 10 |
| `TestAssertion` | NoBrokenCodeExpectation, NoRedundantAssertInstanceOf, PhpUnitMockApi | 10 |
| `TestClass` | ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClass, NoControlFlowInTestMethod, NoHelperMethodInTestClass, SrcUnitTestPair, TestNamingConvention | 18 |
| `Shared` | 既存のまま（`phpstan.neon` が `Shared/FileTokenParser.php` を名指すため） | 19 |

`tests/Unit/PhpStan/Rule` も同じ8カテゴリに揃えました。

制約が2つあり、それが形を決めました。**ルールクラス自体は直下に残す必要があります** — `extension.neon` が `PhpAiToolkit\PhpStan\Rule\<Name>Rule` を名指しており、PSR-4でファイル位置が固定されるためです（かつ当該ファイルは編集できません）。また **`tree.yaml` の `max_depth: 3`** により、カテゴリの下にさらにルール別ディレクトリは置けません。したがってカテゴリはファイルを直接持つ形にしました。コラボレータのクラス名はもともとルール間で重複がなく、リネームは発生していません。

## もう一点、私の前コミットの欠陥を修正しました

`composer.json` から `infection` / `infection:pr` / `infection:coverage` の3スクリプトが失われていました。前コミット（`97877cd`）で落ちており、`composer infection` が「Command "infection" is not defined」で動かない状態でした。ミューテーションゲートが実行不能になっていたということです。復元し、実際に走らせて確認しました。

## ゲート結果
